![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14273381/assets/8aacb12bf70c7588288652b43a3168ae7c00bd8c19a720475c0eda31045a73e8.png)

Consider the region that lies above the $x$-axis (shown in the picture) bounded by the curve $f(y)=2{y}^{2}-{y}^{3}$ and the $y$-axis. Using the shell method, calculate the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $y$-axis by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-{y}^{3} & =0 \\ {y}^{2}(2-y) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=0,$ and $y=2,$ since we are only concerned about values that lie above the $x$-axis. So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=2.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}yf(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}y(2{y}^{2}-{y}^{3})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(2{y}^{3}-{y}^{4})\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi (2\cdot {\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{2}-{\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}|}_{0}^{2}) \\  & =2\pi (2(\frac{16}{4}-0)-(\frac{32}{5}-0)) \\  & =2\pi (8-\frac{32}{5}) \\  & =\frac{16\pi }{5}\end{aligned}
$$
